column2: On the bus up to Tibidabo, Marc, a reserved locksmith, tells Yuna about the old amusement park. Yuna recalls Martí's fifth letter: one September Sunday in 1978 her grandmother and her little mother rode the red plane while Martí watched from below, and a photo of the three was never collected. Quiet, tender.
calm, a little expectant
explaining plainly on the bus; a dry little joke at the end
soft and moved
quiet, wondering

Yuna and Marc ride the funicular up and walk through the crowded park to the old red plane, L'Avió, from 1928. Marc asks if she is scared; she answers "Pero es igual", reusing words Marc once said on the cable car: then "es igual" meant "it's the same", now she means "it doesn't matter". Then they echo each other: "like your grandfather's clock" / "like my grandfather's clock". Light, a little shy.
light, taking in the view
gently, a short question
a little scared but steady; "es igual" here means "it doesn't matter"
amused, noticing a word change its meaning
quiet pride; "L'Avió" is Catalan, said natively

column2: making the connection, softly

column1: Como el reloj de mi abuelo.
column2: repeating her words back, agreeing quietly

Yuna and Marc ride the red plane high over Barcelona. Yuna admits she is really afraid this time; Marc says nothing and lays his hand on hers without holding it. She thinks of her grandmother and mother on this same plane 48 years ago, and of Martí's grandson beside her now. Hushed and intimate.
hushed, a little afraid
truly afraid this time, small voice
quiet and tender

On a bench at the edge of the mountain, Marc, who rarely talks about himself, tells Yuna that his grandfather Martí rode the plane alone every September, "because here I was happy one day". He uses the Catalan word "avi" (grandfather). Yuna gives him the letter; they wonder if the old photo still exists. Quiet, a small turn toward hope at the end.

column1: Yo venía aquí con mi abuelo.
column2: looking at the city, remembering, unhurried
echoing the word, curious
plain and low; a little fond at "No hablaba mucho"
a small, gentle tease
dry agreement, almost smiling
quiet, quoting his grandfather; "Avi" is Catalan for grandpa
quietly, folding the letter
a soft echo, agreeing
a quiet idea, not smiling but hopeful
